samples.summary: bin.test.ts mocks away the entire module under test's only dependency and asserts only that a mock was called
samples.evidence: `vi.mock('../src/cli.js', () => ({ runCli, buildProgram: vi.fn() }))` replaces the whole entrypoint implementation; the test's assertions are `expect(runCli).toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` and `expect(runCli).toHaveBeenCalledWith()` (bin.test.ts:17-20). Nothing about the real CLI can fail this test — it only pins the one-line shape of `void runCli()` in src/bin.ts:6. It is also blind to the fact that bin discards the returned promise (`void`), so it would pass unchanged if runCli's rejection path were unhandled. The substantive behavior is covered in output.test.ts, so this is coverage-shape, not a missing behavior.

samples.summary: No test exercises runCli's default-parameter path (`runCli()` with no program and no argv) — exactly the call shape the shipped binary uses
samples.evidence: Every runCli invocation in tests passes an explicit program and argv (output.test.ts:343, 361), and bin.test.ts stubs runCli entirely, so `program: Command = buildProgram()` / `parseAsync(undefined)` in src/cli.ts:50-54 is never executed. A failure in that default path (e.g. buildProgram throwing during default-arg evaluation, whose rejection `void runCli()` in bin.ts:6 would silently swallow) would leave the whole suite green. `buildProgram()` is tested only in isolation (output.test.ts:369) and never through runCli.

samples.summary: `expect(process.exitCode).toBe(0)` in the success test is trivially true
samples.evidence: `beforeEach` sets `process.exitCode = 0` (output.test.ts:318) and only `outputError` would change it, which the preceding `expect(stderrSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` already rules out. The assertion cannot independently fail; harmless but not coverage.

samples.summary: Local helper `buildProgram()` shadows the newly imported `buildProgram` from src/cli.ts
samples.evidence: output.test.ts:8 imports `buildProgram` from '../src/cli.js', while line 233 declares a different local `buildProgram()` (docs+sheets only) used by `run()`. They happen to be in different describe scopes, so the wiring test at line 369 does use the imported one, but the name collision makes it easy to later move a test into the wrong scope and silently assert against the two-command stub instead of the real program.

finding.summary: `bin entrypoint` tests assert on source text, not behavior; one assertion is vacuous
finding.evidence: The `bin entrypoint` describe (test/output.test.ts:303-318) `readFileSync`s src/bin.ts and string-matches it. `expect(source).toContain('outputError')` is satisfied by the import on bin.ts:13 (and by the word inside the comment on bin.ts:33) regardless of whether the catch handler calls it — it passes even if the catch body were `{}`. `expect(source).toMatch(/\.catch\(/)` matches any `.catch(` anywhere in the file, on any promise. Likewise `toContain('program.parseAsync(')` / `not.toMatch(/program\.parse\s*\(/)` pass for aliased calls (`const p = program; p.parse()`) or a `parseAsync(...)` whose promise is never awaited/handled. The claimed behavior — a rejection escaping an action handler is turned into the `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope with exit 1 — is never executed, so these two tests are presented as coverage of bin.ts but cannot fail if that behavior breaks.

verdict.reason: The finding describes source-text assertions that do not exist in this repository. `packages/cli/test/output.test.ts` contains no `readFileSync` and no string-matching of `src/bin.ts`; a repo-wide grep for `toContain('outputError')` and `program.parse\s*(` returns zero matches. Lines 303-318 are a comment plus a `beforeEach`, inside `describe('runCli entrypoint')`, not a `bin entrypoint` describe. `src/bin.ts` is 6 lines total with no `outputError` import, no `.catch(`, and no `parseAsync(` — the quoted bin.ts:13/bin.ts:33 evidence cannot exist. Moreover, the behavior the finding says is never executed IS executed: output.test.ts:341-352 invokes the real `runCli` (src/cli.ts:49-58, unmocked) with an action that rejects after a microtask and asserts the stderr envelope equals `{code:'LATE_FAILURE', message:'kaboom'}` with exitCode 1 — that assertion fails under a synchronous `parse()`. The only `describe('bin entrypoint')` is test/bin.test.ts:13-22, which imports the real bin module with `../src/cli.js` mocked and asserts `runCli` was called once with no args; it does no source-text matching. Ground: not-present.

finding.summary: No behavioral test for the new `parseAsync().catch(outputError)` entrypoint path
finding.evidence: bin.ts:35-37 is the new behavior (unhandled action rejection → error envelope + exitCode 1). The only test touching it is the source-string describe at test/output.test.ts:303. I searched packages/cli/test for any import or execution of bin.ts (grep for 'bin', 'parseAsync', 'spawn', 'execFile' across packages/cli/test) and found only the readFileSync source check; no test registers a command whose action rejects outside its own try/catch and asserts the envelope/exit code. A test could register a throwing action on a program and await `parseAsync().catch(outputError)`-equivalent wiring, or exercise a real command whose failure path escapes the handler (e.g. getConfig/getClient throwing before the try).

verdict.reason: Refuted by direct counterexample: the exact test the finding says is missing exists and is behavioral, not vacuous. output.test.ts:331-339 defines programWithRejectingAction() — a `boom` command whose async action awaits a microtask then throws LateFailure outside any try/catch — and :341-352 passes it to the REAL, unmocked runCli (imported from ../src/cli.js at output.test.ts:8, i.e. the actual `try { await program.parseAsync(...) } catch { outputError(e) }` at cli.ts:53-57), then asserts the parsed stderr envelope equals { code: 'LATE_FAILURE', message: 'kaboom' } (:346-350) AND process.exitCode === 1 (:351). Only console.log/console.error are spied; createProgram and outputError are real, so no over-mocking. The test is falsifiable: under synchronous parse() commander drops the action promise, the rejection escapes the catch, stderr is never called and exitCode stays 0, failing :346/:351. A negative control at :354-366 asserts a successful run leaves exitCode 0 and stderr untouched. Additionally the finding's cited location is wrong: src/bin.ts is only 6 lines with no parseAsync/catch at 35-37 — it is `void runCli()` (bin.ts:6), and cli.ts:45-47 documents that the logic was moved out of bin.ts precisely to make this path testable; that delegation is covered by test/bin.test.ts:14-21. The reviewer's claim that output.test.ts:303 is a 'source-string describe' is also incorrect: :303 is a comment line in the explanatory header for the behavioral `runCli entrypoint` suite beginning at :306, and no readFileSync source check exists there.
